source.title: LLM-Guided Initialization for Accelerated Hybrid Quantum-Classical Medical Image Classification
source.authors: Riza Alaudin Syah; Irwan Alnarus Kautsar; Haza Nuzly Bin Abdull Hamed

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: Tests LLM-guided initialization in a hybrid quantum-classical image classifier, a new model setting for initialization and trainability results. The study does not test the specified classical-network versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own gradient-variance, training-time and accuracy outcomes for quantum circuits. These concern initialization and trainability in quantum circuits, but none measures the classical-network behavior named by the versions.
record.test_reason: The study tests initialization and gradient variance in parameterized quantum circuits, whereas V1–V6 name classical neural-network behaviors. Its classical CNN comparator reports accuracy without identifying the evaluation split or testing any specified optimization behavior. Related quantum results do not constitute a T3 test of these versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion as a reported result: single-query AdaInit gives a stated 14.6× increase in initial gradient variance and a 160× CUDA-Q training speedup at the same reported 61.4% accuracy. They present deeper-circuit training benefits as future work. The variance multiplier is inconsistent with the displayed numbers, and equal final accuracy alone does not establish their asserted global optimum or single dominant basin.
record.recipe_differences: A single-query LLM initialization for a variational quantum circuit, followed by Adam training; the claim versions concern classical neural networks and other methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports backend-dependent training times: CUDA-Q and PennyLane differ for AdaInit. It also reports gradient-variance decay across random-initialized circuit depths.

fits_no_version.finding: In the four-qubit, two-layer quantum model, Table I reports initial gradient variance of 0.0095 with AdaInit versus 0.0006 with random initialization. The stated 14.6× ratio is inconsistent with those displayed values.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM-guided initialization increases the reported initial gradient variance in the tested shallow quantum classifier.

fits_no_version.finding: Table II reports CUDA-Q training times of 1.1 seconds with AdaInit and 176 seconds with random initialization, both at 61.4% accuracy. AdaInit with PennyLane takes 82 seconds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AdaInit reduces reported training time in this shallow quantum classifier, with timing dependent on the backend.

fits_no_version.finding: Random-initialized quantum-circuit gradient variance falls from 0.0626 at two layers to 0.0225 at eight layers, a reported 64% decay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The measured gradient variance decreases with depth in the tested randomly initialized quantum circuits.

fits_no_version.finding: The classical CNN comparator reports 100% accuracy versus 61.4% for the quantum models, without specifying the accuracy evaluation split.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The classical comparator achieves higher reported classification accuracy than the tested shallow quantum models on DMR-IR.

record.problems: The experiments use one dataset and task and focus on shallow circuits; the authors describe barren plateaus as relatively mild at the tested 2-layer depth. Gradient variance is reported as a scalar aggregate. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper's claims about deeper circuits are presented as expectations or future work, not demonstrated training results.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying reported results were omitted.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large classical convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and model-size or training-recipe effects.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training degradation with classical convolutional-network depth, identity residual shortcuts, and the specified initialization and normalization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, training speed and trainable depth in plain classical networks; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Learning-rate stability limits, transient loss growth, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability behavior and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and tolerated learning rates, and normalization-free Fixup residual training.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels apply. The gradient-variance metric is variance across parameter components at an initialization, not a reported variance across repeated random initializations. Figure 2's caption describes an AdaInit-versus-random depth comparison, while Table III contains only random initialization and deeper training remains future work; this does not supply evidence for any specified version.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, early stopping and regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual classical convolutional networks, depth effects, identity shortcuts, Fixup and normalization.
Classical plain networks, activation-matched initializations, signal and gradient propagation across layers, and training at greater depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss increases or divergence, curvature and sharpness during training.
Batch normalization versus no normalization in the listed classical networks and tasks.
